title: Show overflowing tabs: keep the active chip visible and add a +N list
body:
Since card czysfd, every dispatched worker after the first stacks as a tab in ONE half-width window, so a plan run routinely has more tabs than fit. `header_layout` (src/wm.rs, pure rect math) silently stops packing chips when out of room ("cycling still reaches the hidden tabs"): no "+N", no sign. Seen in the czysfd screenshot: 4 workers stacked, only worker 1-3 chips drawn, worker 4 visible only in the Sessions panel. Because packing always starts at tab 0, an active tab past the fit has no chip at all, and a bell ringing on a hidden tab pulses nothing in the header.

DESIGN (decided; if you find it wrong, `kanban block` with the reason rather than switching silently):
1. The active tab always has a visible chip. Pack from tab 0 when the active tab fits; otherwise slide the window so the active chip is the last one that fits (a stable, predictable rule; no animation, no scroll state).
2. When any tab is hidden, reserve room for one overflow chip "+N" at the end of the strip (before the `+` / control zone), where N = hidden count. Its width is reserved BEFORE packing so it never overlaps the controls. No overflow -> layout is byte-for-byte today's (existing header_layout tests must pass unchanged).
3. Clicking "+N" opens a popup list of the hidden tabs: icon, title, and the same agent-state badge the Sessions panel paints (reuse its painter; do not add a second badge style). Clicking a row activates that tab exactly as clicking its chip would (same focus behaviour as a chip click). Escape or a click outside closes it. While open, keys must not reach the terminal.
4. The "+N" chip pulses with the bell colour when any hidden tab's bell is active (same `bell_pulse` as chips), and shows the needs-you colour when any hidden tab's agent state is NeedsYou. That is the orchestration case: a hidden worker waiting on you must be visible without opening the Sessions panel.
5. Applies to every tab stack (terminals, projects, viewers), not only dispatched workers.

OUT OF SCOPE: horizontal scrolling of the strip, shrinking chips below today's sizes, drag-reordering in the popup, agent-state badges on regular chips.

DONE WHEN:
- header_layout stays pure; table tests for: no overflow (unchanged rects), overflow with active inside the fit, overflow with active past the fit (active chip visible, correct hidden count), a single very narrow window (one chip, no panic, degenerate widths total), and the reserved "+N" rect never overlapping the control zone.
- A wm test: activating a hidden tab via the popup's action path selects it and leaves focus as a chip click would.
- egui ids for the popup are unique per window across nested Projects (see egui-immediate-mode-reference: duplicate widget Ids across nested Projects).
- docs/window-chrome.md gains a short overflow section (rule 1, the +N chip, why: dispatch stacking).
- GUI claim: one inspected screenshot of a 6-tab stack in a half-width window with the active tab past the fit and the popup open. Screenshots are user-only: write a script like the czysfd one (sandboxed APPDATA, the instance's own FOREMAN_PIPE, `foreman open` to make tabs, PrintWindow, stop only that pid; never mouse/keyboard) and ask the human in chat to run it.

Gate: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --target-dir target/agent; cargo test --target-dir target/agent. Follow foreman-architecture-contract (local vs screen rects) and egui-immediate-mode-reference.
